<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

Rust only. Delivery: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs ~L231-260 (socket_available → fresh_injection_verdict → select_rung). u1: branch on recipient.harness — for Omp|Pi skip the verdict entirely and hand to the transport (the extension event stream; confirm which Transport impl serves omp in crates/transport and that it buffers a steer during a turn). Keep select_rung pure; add the harness gate one level up. u2: a notice scheduler in the drain (crates/daemon/src/delivery or pointer/worker.rs pattern) that, for rows pending > notice_after_secs (config.rs), enqueues a control message to the SENDER seat (from `pij-rs`, body `still queued: …`), once per row, and `delivered late` on completion when delay > threshold; CLI prints outstanding notices on stderr (crates/cli/src/main.rs, like the stale-card warning). Wire additive only.

<a id="isolation"></a>

## Isolation

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| mode | solo-pm in the plan worktree |
| note | Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence. |
